interest.name: Pandas for reports
interest.wantToLearn: Use Python for data analysis at work
interest.whyText: I rebuild the same Excel reports every month and want to automate them, then do analysis Excel can't.
interest.experienceText: I write small Python scripts for file renaming and API calls. Never used pandas; strong in Excel pivots and VLOOKUP.
successOutcomes: My monthly report runs from one script
I can answer a question my manager asks without rebuilding a spreadsheet
interest.approachNotes: You already think in tables and write Python, so skip language basics and map pandas onto what you do in Excel: filters, pivots, lookups. Work on your own report data from the start, with worked examples you then adapt. The shift that matters is from clicking to describing a transformation in code you can rerun, so each session should end with a script that does one real step of your monthly report.

approachBrief.practice: Write a short pandas step against a copy of their own monthly report file, run it, and check the result against the Excel version.
goodLooksLike: Checks row counts before and after every join
Reruns the script on a new month without edits
Reaches for column operations, not row loops
pitfalls: Looping over rows like a script instead of using vectorized column operations.
Silent join mistakes that duplicate or drop rows, unnoticed without row-count checks.
Copying notebook snippets that work once but can't be rerun on next month's file.
progressionPrinciples: Anchor each pandas idea to the Excel operation it replaces before going beyond Excel.
Loading, selecting and filtering come before grouping, joining and reshaping.
Move from one-off exploration to a rerunnable script early, then build on it.

goals.title: Load and filter your report like Excel filters
Replace formulas with vectorized column calculations
Summarize data like a pivot table
Merge data from several files without losing rows
Reshape a summary into a pivot table layout
Turn your steps into a script you can rerun
Answer an ad hoc question without rebuilding a spreadsheet
